newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak c.bank raises repo rate, cuts rev repo.
newsitem.headline: Slovak c.bank raises repo rate, cuts rev repo.

text.p: The National Bank of Slovakia (NBS) on Thursday said it had raised its bill repurchase rate by 50 basis points to 8.70 percent.
The NBS added that it had also cut its reverse repo rate by 20 basis points to 7.20 percent.
"By extending the repo spread, the NBS is expressing its preference for longer-term liquidity sterilisation," Peter Andresic, NBS chief dealer, told Reuters.
"We further realise that the yield of 9.3 percent on our liquidity bills was not sufficient," he added.

The NBS held a bill auction of an unspecified tranche of three month liquidity bills on Wednesday, but failed to attract bids as dealers complained the central bank's yield expectations were much lower than the market's.
Most banks, according to dealers, submitted bids at around 10 percent.
It was the sixteenth time this year there were no bids at an NBS bill auction, or all had been rejected.
Three-month liquidity bills are the NBS' main instrument for sterilising the money supply.
Andresic said the repo rate hike showed the NBS was reacting to the higher accepted yield in finance ministry treasury bills.
Slovak interbank money rates continued their downtrend over the past week to a bid range of 11.5-12.8 percent on all terms.
"The widened spread will force banks to participate in NBS auctions, and funds will get more expensive," Pavol Kruk, a money dealer at Istrobanka, said.
